edit_distance_threshold.value_status: UNSET — see ADR-010; until it is decided the validator judges structure only, not the threshold

notes: ADR-010 / Bert ruling 1: the 20 existing masks (18 algorithmic:matting + 2 ai:google-ai-mode-nano-banana, only a red-overlay visual check) are NOT grandfathered. Their old values are void; this ticket does not re-make them and does not edit manifest.json.

All 20 slots start as pending. 0/20 point-reviewed and the edit-distance threshold is UNSET, so U1 is UNMET and E1-T4 stays blocked. Changing a status is not what unblocks U1: the last step is a human sign-off, and exit 0 from the validator only means the register is structurally valid.

A reviewed record must satisfy BOTH conditions: mask_source fully matches ^ai-assisted:(?P<model>[a-z0-9_-]+)\+point-reviewed$ AND this register carries the proposal model/version, both sha256 digests, the edit-distance record and the review record. A hand prefix with an AI proposal is a hard conflict.

The model slug forbids '.', ';', ',' and ':'; regression_gate.py's _MASK_SOURCE_RE truncates at those characters. Full version strings (e.g. 2.1) belong in proposal.model_version, never in the prefix.
Pixel-equivalent artefacts (a hash of a re-encoded copy, a size-only comparison, a red-overlay screenshot) are NOT evidence of a point review. See ADR-010, N2.

Field semantics for B2: edit_distance.method=xor@128; changed_pixels=count_nonzero((proposal>=128) XOR (reviewed>=128)), written as XOR not an IoU union/intersection expression; changed_ratio=changed_pixels/(H*W) with the WHOLE FRAME as denominator (not union, not garment region); both sha256 values are hashlib.sha256(Path(mask_path).read_bytes()).hexdigest() over the raw PNG file bytes (RAW PNG BYTES), never a binarised ndarray. File hash proves identity, XOR proves pixel change; re-encoding changes bytes but not pixels, so the hash is not a pixel-equivalence judgement. A shape mismatch is a named failing check, never a silent resize. See ADR-010 section 5.

CI has no manifest.json, so the default validator run checks only the register's own consistency and the expected_ids<->records reconciliation. --cross-check-manifest is a local-only, read-only addition; CI cannot independently verify that this committable index matches the local manifest (D1 residual).

D2 residual (distinct from D1): CI can never independently recompute the pixel edit distance. Its baseline is the AI-proposed mask's pixels at masks_draft/<id>.png, excluded by .git/info/exclude and absent from a clean clone; committing pixels or any pixel-equivalent (RLE, base64 bitmap, downsampled array) is ruled out by N2. B1 declarative summary is the CI default, B2 --verify-local-masks is local/human-run only; neither cryptographically proves a human review. See ADR-010 section 3.
No binary, photo, mask or manifest.json value is stored in this directory. It ships in git so a clean clone can mechanically judge register completeness.
